title: Direct Identification via Government ID
description: Government ID and name provided during registration can directly identify the parent user, enabling identification without additional authentication.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Registration Data
description: Email, password, name, government ID, and six-digit code could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, insider threats, or inadequate access controls.

title: Linkability of Registration Data to Other Data Sources
description: Registration data (especially government ID and email) could be linked to other data sources, creating a comprehensive profile of the parent user across systems.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance in Data Handling
description: Collection and storage of government ID and sensitive personal data may not comply with data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) if proper consent, minimization, and retention policies are not implemented.

title: Identifiability of Parent Account Data
description: The MongoDB users collection stores parent account information that can be used to identify individuals. If accessed by unauthorized parties, this data could reveal personal identities and account relationships.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Parent Account Data
description: Parent account data stored in MongoDB could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, insufficient encryption, or security vulnerabilities in the database system.

title: Data Integrity Compromise of Parent Account
description: Parent account data in MongoDB could be tampered with or modified by unauthorized actors, leading to authentication failures, account hijacking, or incorrect parent-child relationship mappings.

title: Linkability of Parent Account Data
description: Parent account data processed by the Authentication Service could be linked to other data flows or systems, potentially enabling correlation attacks that reveal additional information about users.

title: Usurpation of Parent Account Identity
description: The Authentication Service could be vulnerable to identity usurpation attacks where unauthorized actors attempt to impersonate parent accounts, potentially through credential theft or session hijacking.

title: User Identifiability via JWT and User Data
description: The JWT token and associated user data transmitted from the Authentication Service to the Parent User can directly identify the individual, potentially exposing personally identifiable information (PII) to unauthorized parties if intercepted or mishandled.
assumptions: JWT contains user identity claims; user data includes PII

title: Data Disclosure During Transmission
description: User data and JWT tokens transmitted from the Authentication Service to the Parent User may be exposed to interception or unauthorized disclosure if the communication channel is not properly secured (e.g., lacking TLS encryption).
assumptions: Transmission may occur over unencrypted or weakly encrypted channels

title: JWT Token Usurpation and Impersonation
description: An attacker who obtains the JWT token could potentially impersonate the authenticated user to the Parent User system, gaining unauthorized access to resources or performing actions on behalf of the legitimate user.
assumptions: JWT tokens are not properly validated or have insufficient expiration controls

title: Excessive Data Minimization Violation
description: The flow transmits 'JWT + user data' which may include more information than necessary for the Parent User to perform its function, potentially violating data minimization principles and increasing privacy risk.
assumptions: User data may contain sensitive fields not required for the parent user's access

title: Parent User Identifiability of End User
description: The Parent User receiving JWT and user data may be able to identify the end user, creating privacy risks if the Parent User is not a trusted entity or if the data is further shared or stored.
assumptions: Parent User has access to user identity information; Parent User may not be fully trusted

title: Linkability of Child Login to Parent Identity
description: The child's login activity using parent credentials can be linked to the parent's identity through the parent email, creating a connection between the child's online activities and the parent's personal information.
assumptions: The authentication service logs and stores parent email associated with child login events.

title: Identification of Parent-Child Relationship
description: The parent email and password used for child authentication can identify the parent-child relationship, potentially revealing sensitive family information to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Parent email is unique and identifiable, and the system does not mask this information.

title: Disclosure of Credentials in Transit
description: Parent email and password transmitted during child login could be intercepted by network attackers, leading to unauthorized access to the parent's account.
assumptions: Transmission may not be adequately encrypted or protected.

title: Excessive Data Collection for Child Authentication
description: Collecting parent email and password for child login may exceed what is necessary for authentication purposes, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Child authentication could potentially use alternative methods that don't require parent credentials.

title: Usurpation of Parent Account via Child Login
description: If child credentials are compromised, attackers could potentially usurp the parent's account, gaining unauthorized access to parent's personal data and services.
assumptions: Child login credentials are stored or transmitted in a way that could be compromised.

title: Child User Identifiable from JWT and Profile Data
description: The JWT token and child profile data transmitted from the Authentication Service to the Child User contain personally identifiable information that could be used to identify the child user to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: JWT tokens and child profiles contain PII fields that are not properly anonymized or pseudonymized.

title: JWT Token Interception During Transmission
description: JWT tokens transmitted from the Authentication Service to the Child User could be intercepted by network attackers, leading to unauthorized access to child user accounts and sensitive profile information.
assumptions: Transmission channel may not be adequately secured with encryption or token validation mechanisms.

title: Child User Impersonation via Compromised JWT
description: If JWT tokens are stolen or compromised, attackers could impersonate the child user to access protected resources or perform unauthorized actions on their behalf.
assumptions: JWT tokens are not properly validated, have insufficient expiration, or lack proper signature verification.

title: Excessive Data in Child Profile Transmission
description: The child profile data transmitted may contain more personal information than necessary for the authentication service's purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Child profiles include fields that are not strictly required for authentication or service functionality.

title: Child User Data Linkable Across Systems
description: The JWT and child profile data received by the Child User could be linked with other data sources (e.g., other services, devices, or online activities) to create a comprehensive profile of the child user.
assumptions: Child User may have access to or share data with other systems that could be correlated with this authentication data.

title: Linkability of Government ID to Other Data Sources
description: The government ID provided during child profile creation could be linked with other data sources (e.g., school records, medical records) to create a comprehensive profile of the child, potentially revealing sensitive information beyond the intended scope.
assumptions: Data is stored in systems that can be cross-referenced with external databases

title: Direct Identification of Child Through Profile Data
description: The combination of name, DOB, gender, and government ID in the child profile enables direct identification of the child, which could be misused for tracking or surveillance purposes.
assumptions: Profile data is accessible to authorized personnel and potentially stored in centralized systems

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Government ID
description: Government ID information stored in the child profile could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system breaches, insider threats, or improper access controls.
assumptions: Access controls may not be sufficient to prevent unauthorized access to sensitive data

title: Tampering with Child Profile Data
description: The child profile data could be altered or tampered with by unauthorized actors, leading to incorrect information being used for identification or decision-making purposes.
assumptions: Data integrity controls may not be robust enough to prevent unauthorized modifications

title: Child Profile Creation by Unauthorized Person
description: An unauthorized person could impersonate the parent or child to create a false profile, potentially leading to identity theft or misuse of the child's information.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may not be strong enough to verify the identity of the parent creating the profile

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance in Child Data Processing
description: The child profile management process may not comply with data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, COPPA) regarding the collection, storage, and processing of children's personal data.
assumptions: Organizational policies and technical controls may not fully align with regulatory requirements

title: Unauthorized Access to Child Profile Data
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB collection could be accessed by unauthorized parties if access controls are insufficient, exposing sensitive personal information about children.

title: Unauthorized Modification of Child Profile Data
description: Child profile data could be altered by unauthorized actors, leading to incorrect or malicious changes to sensitive child information.

title: Direct Identification of Children
description: Child profile data contains personally identifiable information that could be used to directly identify children, creating privacy risks.

title: Linkability of Child Data to Other Sources
description: Child profile data could be linked with other datasets to create comprehensive profiles, increasing privacy risks through data correlation.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Child Data
description: Child profile management may violate child-specific data protection regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other applicable laws requiring special safeguards for minors.

title: Linkability of Video Search and Interaction History
description: The child user's video search queries, likes, and comments can be linked across sessions and contexts, potentially revealing patterns of interest and behavior that could be used to build a profile of the user.
assumptions: User activity is logged and stored in a way that allows correlation across different interactions.

title: Identification Through Behavioral Patterns
description: Video search patterns, comment content, and like behavior could be used to identify the child user, especially if combined with other data sources or if the user is a minor with limited anonymity.
assumptions: Behavioral data is sufficient for identification, especially for child users who may have limited digital footprint.

title: Disclosure of Video Content and User Interactions
description: Video content accessed through the search and comment features could be disclosed to unauthorized parties, including other users, service providers, or third parties through data sharing or breaches.
assumptions: Video content and interaction data may be stored, shared, or accessible beyond the intended user.

title: Excessive Data Collection on Video Interactions
description: The system may collect more data than necessary for the video search, request, like, and comment functionality, including detailed search history, comment metadata, and interaction timestamps that are not essential for the service.
assumptions: Data collection practices are not minimized to what is strictly necessary for the stated functionality.

title: Usurpation Through Account Compromise
description: A child user's account could be compromised, allowing an attacker to impersonate the user, post comments, or like videos on their behalf, potentially leading to unauthorized representation and privacy violations.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be insufficient to prevent account takeover, especially for child users.

title: Non-Compliance with Child Privacy Regulations
description: The Video Management Service may not comply with child privacy regulations (such as COPPA or GDPR-K) regarding data collection, storage, and processing of child user data, including video interactions and search history.
assumptions: The service may not have adequate safeguards or legal compliance measures for child user data.

title: Linkability of Video Metadata to Individuals
description: Video metadata may contain identifying information (names, timestamps, locations) that can be linked to specific individuals, enabling correlation of video content with personal activities.
assumptions: Metadata includes personally identifiable information

title: Identification of Individuals Through Video Content
description: Video files stored in MongoDB may contain visual or audio content that can be used to identify individuals, including faces, voices, or other biometric characteristics.
assumptions: Video content contains identifiable features

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Video Data
description: Video files and metadata in the MongoDB collection may be accessed by unauthorized parties through security vulnerabilities, misconfigured access controls, or insider threats.
assumptions: Access controls may be insufficient

title: Excessive Video Data Collection
description: The Video Management Service may collect and store video data beyond what is necessary for its intended purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Data collection scope exceeds business requirements

title: Usurpation of Video Access Rights
description: Unauthorized users may gain access to video content through credential theft, session hijacking, or privilege escalation, leading to improper access to sensitive video data.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be compromised

title: Unauthorized Access to Child Search and Watch History
description: Child search and watch history stored in MongoDB childprofiles collection could be accessed by unauthorized parties, potentially revealing sensitive information about children's interests, preferences, and online behavior patterns.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls, authentication, or encryption on the MongoDB data store

title: Child Identity Inference from Behavioral Patterns
description: Analysis of search and watch history patterns could enable identification of specific children, their age groups, interests, or even family characteristics, potentially leading to profiling or targeted manipulation.
assumptions: Pattern analysis techniques exist that can link behavioral data to individual identities

title: Excessive Collection of Child Behavioral Data
description: The Child Profile Management process may collect more data than necessary for its stated purpose, storing detailed search and watch history that exceeds what is needed for basic profile management functions.
assumptions: Data minimization principles are not fully applied during system design

title: Potential Violation of Child Privacy Regulations
description: Collection and storage of child search and watch history may violate COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child-specific privacy regulations requiring explicit parental consent, data minimization, and strict access controls for minor data.
assumptions: Current implementation does not fully comply with applicable child privacy laws

title: Video Content Identifies User
description: Video content uploaded by the parent user may contain personally identifiable information (PII) such as facial features, voice patterns, or contextual details that can directly identify the user to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Video content is processed and stored without adequate anonymization or masking techniques.

title: Cross-Platform Linkability of Video Data
description: Video data uploaded to the Video Management Service may be linked to the user across different platforms, services, or time periods, enabling profiling and tracking of user behavior.
assumptions: Video metadata or content is shared or accessible across multiple systems without proper isolation.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Video Data
description: Video data may be disclosed to unauthorized third parties during processing, storage, or transmission, potentially violating user privacy expectations and consent.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls, encryption, or audit mechanisms exist in the Video Management Service.

title: Video Data Tampering During Processing
description: Video data may be altered, corrupted, or tampered with during upload, processing, or storage by malicious actors or system vulnerabilities.
assumptions: Insufficient integrity checks, digital signatures, or encryption mechanisms are in place.

title: Unclear Consent Mechanisms for Video Upload
description: The approval/rejection process may lack clear, understandable consent mechanisms, making it difficult for users to understand how their video data will be used, stored, or shared.
assumptions: Privacy notices and consent forms are not user-friendly or transparent.

title: Child identification from video stream
description: The video stream may contain identifiable information about the child, including facial features, voice, or other biometric data that could be used to identify the child.

title: Unauthorized access to video stream
description: The video stream could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission, potentially exposing the child's activities or location.

title: Linking video data to child identity
description: Video data from the stream could be linked to the child's identity through metadata, timestamps, or other identifiers, creating a comprehensive profile.

title: Child impersonation in video access
description: An unauthorized party could potentially impersonate the child to access or receive the video stream, bypassing authentication controls.

title: Linkability of child browsing data across sessions
description: Child browsing data from MongoDB collection could be linked across different sessions or platforms, creating a comprehensive behavioral profile of the child that exceeds the intended scope of the AI recommendation engine.
assumptions: Data is retained across sessions and linked by child identifier

title: Identification of child from browsing data
description: Child browsing data may contain sufficient information to identify the specific child, especially when combined with other data sources or metadata, violating child privacy expectations.
assumptions: Browsing data includes or can be correlated with identifying information

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child browsing data
description: Child browsing data transmitted to the AI engine could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data breaches, insider threats, or improper access controls.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network and stored in AI engine

title: Excessive data collection by AI engine
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may collect and process more child browsing data than necessary for generating recommendations, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: AI engine has broad data access and retention policies

title: Non-compliance with child data protection regulations
description: Processing of child browsing data may violate GDPR, COPPA, or other child privacy regulations due to inadequate consent mechanisms, data retention policies, or parental oversight.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements apply to child data processing

title: Linkability of Browsing Data Across Systems
description: Browsing data sent to third-party advertisers may be linked with other data sources (e.g., cookies, device IDs) to create comprehensive user profiles, enabling tracking across multiple platforms and services.
assumptions: Advertisers have access to additional data sources for cross-referencing
uncertainty_note: Node L.1.1 is a reasonable fit for cross-system linking threats in LINDDUN Pro

title: Indirect Identification Through Browsing Behavior
description: Browsing data patterns can be used to indirectly identify individuals through behavioral profiling, even if direct identifiers are removed, potentially revealing sensitive preferences, health interests, or political views.
assumptions: Advertisers can correlate browsing patterns with known user identities
uncertainty_note: Node I.1.2 represents indirect identification through profiling; alternative could be I.1.1 for direct identification

title: Over-Disclosure of Browsing Data
description: More browsing data is shared with advertisers than necessary for the stated purpose, potentially exposing sensitive user information beyond what's needed for ad targeting.
assumptions: Data minimization principles are not fully implemented
uncertainty_note: Node D.1.1 fits over-disclosure; D.1.2 could also apply if unauthorized parties receive data

title: Deception About Data Usage and Collection
description: Users may be misled about how their browsing data is collected, stored, and used by third-party advertisers, as consent mechanisms may not fully inform users of the extent of data sharing.
assumptions: Privacy policies are complex or users do not read them
uncertainty_note: Node Dd.1.1 represents misleading about data collection; Dd.1.2 could apply for misleading about usage

title: GDPR/Privacy Regulation Non-Compliance
description: Sharing browsing data with third-party advertisers may violate GDPR or other privacy regulations if proper consent, data subject rights, or data processing agreements are not established.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements are not fully met for third-party data sharing
uncertainty_note: Node Nc.1.1 represents GDPR compliance; Nc.1.2 could apply for other regulations

title: Direct Identification via Government ID Images
description: Government ID images contain personally identifiable information that directly identifies individuals, making them highly sensitive to identification attacks.

title: Linkability of ID Images to Other Data
description: Stored government ID images can be linked to other personal data sources, enabling comprehensive profiling of individuals.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored ID Images
description: File system storing government ID images may be accessible by unauthorized parties, leading to privacy breaches.

title: Data Manipulation of ID Images
description: Stored government ID images could be altered or tampered with, compromising their authenticity and integrity.

title: Identity Theft via Stolen ID Images
description: If ID images are compromised, they could be used for identity theft, impersonation, or fraudulent activities.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance in ID Storage
description: Storing government ID images may violate data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA) if proper safeguards are not implemented.

title: JWT Token Disclosure via XSS Attack
description: JWT tokens stored in localStorage are vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks, allowing attackers to read and exfiltrate authentication tokens through malicious scripts.
assumptions: Attacker has ability to inject malicious scripts into the application

title: User Identity Usurpation via Token Theft
description: Stolen JWT tokens from localStorage can be used by attackers to impersonate legitimate users, gaining unauthorized access to protected resources and performing actions on behalf of the user.
assumptions: Attacker obtains JWT token and has valid session context

title: JWT Token Modification via localStorage Manipulation
description: Attackers with XSS access can modify JWT tokens stored in localStorage, potentially altering claims, extending expiration, or creating fraudulent tokens.
assumptions: Attacker has script injection capability and JWT is not cryptographically signed/verified

title: User Data Linkability Through Token Correlation
description: JWT tokens contain user identifiers and session information that can be correlated with other data sources, enabling profiling and tracking of user activities across services.
assumptions: Multiple data sources exist that can be correlated with token information

title: User Identifiability Through Token Exposure
description: JWT tokens may contain user identifiers (user ID, email, etc.) that are exposed when tokens are stolen or leaked, making users directly identifiable to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: JWT payload contains personally identifiable information (PII)

title: Non-Compliance with Security Best Practices
description: Storing JWT tokens in localStorage violates security best practices and may violate regulatory requirements (e.g., GDPR, OWASP guidelines) that recommend secure storage mechanisms like httpOnly cookies.
assumptions: Organizational security policies and regulations require secure token storage

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child History
description: Child's historical data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, improper access controls, or data breaches, violating the child's privacy expectations.
assumptions: System has access controls that may be bypassed or compromised

title: Child Identification Through History Data
description: Child's history data may contain personally identifiable information that could identify the child to unauthorized parties, even when intended for parent review only.
assumptions: History data may include dates, locations, or activities that could identify the child

title: Excessive Data Display to Parent
description: The system may display more detailed child history information than necessary for the parent's review purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: System displays full history rather than summarized or age-appropriate information

title: Linkability of Child History to Other Data
description: Child's history data could be linked with other data sources (e.g., school records, medical data) to create a comprehensive profile without consent.
assumptions: Data may be accessible across multiple systems or shared with third parties

title: Unauthorized Access to Child Profile Management
description: Parent user account could be compromised, allowing unauthorized individuals to access child's history and profile management functions.
assumptions: Parent credentials may be stolen or system authentication may be weak
